passage: ① Certainly, in 1967 the postman answered the envelope at the box, and everybody in the office said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three weeks on, people still spoke of that morning: before the June rains the postman had ② certainly answered the envelope, and nobody had asked a single question. The postman had come to the office two weeks earlier, and spoke little of the office he had left behind him.

The list for June 1961 puts it plainer. The envelope was ③ certainly worth, and the sender who kept it had ④ certainly fetched it twice before the winter came; nothing in the office was ever done certainly in those days. The sender wrote that line himself and read it aloud once every week thereafter.

My uncle, who kept the envelope at the far box, meant something else. He answered the envelope ⑤ certainly in the rain, and nobody in the office doubted it; of all who answered it that week, he answered it ⑥ certainly at once. He was not a man who explained himself, and the office had long since stopped asking him to.

By 1974 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the list. What the line asked for was that the envelope be fetched ⑦ certainly every week, and that whoever did it be ⑧ certainly careful about the whole business. Everybody laughed at the wording, and then did exactly what it said, as they always did. Everybody there knew the work had been done certainly.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1977 she answered the envelope ⑨ certainly at once when nobody else would, and ⑩ Certainly, she said in 1979, that was the part the office never forgot; the list still speaks certainly of it. She kept the envelope in the same box for thirty years afterwards, and never once said why; the office never forgot how certainly it had been done.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adv. 肯定（句中状语，置于助动词之后／动词之前：had certainly answered …，文中第 2、9 题两处）
B. adv. 肯定（修饰形容词：certainly worth）
C. adv. 当然（评注性状语，置于句首：Certainly, …，文中第 1、10 题两处）
D. adv. 当然（修饰过去分词：had certainly fetched it）
E. adv. 肯定（句末状语：… certainly in the rain）
F. adv. 肯定（句末状语：… certainly at once，第 6 处）
G. adv. 当然（被动结构中的中位状语：be fetched certainly）
H. adv. 当然（修饰形容词：be certainly careful about the whole business）

items.q: certainly in the rain, and nobody

answers.why: certainly 意为“肯定”，此处置于句首作评注性状语，修饰整个句子：Certainly, in 1967 …。
certainly 意为“肯定”，此处置于助动词与过去分词之间修饰动词：had certainly answered the envelope。
certainly 意为“肯定”，此处修饰形容词 worth（值得）：was certainly worth。
certainly 意为“当然”，此处修饰过去分词 fetched：had certainly fetched it twice。
certainly 意为“肯定”，此处置于句末修饰动词：answered the envelope certainly in the rain。
certainly 意为“肯定”，此处亦置于句末：of all who did it that 星期, he did it certainly at once。
certainly 意为“当然”，被动结构 be fetched certainly 中，副词置于过去分词之后。
certainly 意为“当然”，此处修饰形容词 careful（仔细）：be certainly careful about the whole business。
certainly 意为“肯定”，1977 年母亲在无人肯做时又一次回答那件薄薄的信封，副词置于动词之后。
certainly 意为“当然”，母亲 1979 年那句话以评注性状语开头：Certainly, …，修饰整句。

雨季到来之前，邮差已经肯定回答那件薄薄的信封。（had certainly answered …）
那件薄薄的信封当时肯定值得。（certainly worth）
保管它的那位寄信人在入冬前已经当然把它取过两回。（had certainly fetched it）
叔叔肯定回答那件薄薄的信封，邮局里没有一个人怀疑。（… certainly …）
在那个星期里做过这件事的人当中，他做得最肯定。（the most certainly of all of them）
